Decisions this run made

The close calls, and the other reading of each

Every judgment this run flagged as one that could have gone the other way, with what it moved. A grade that rests on one of these is a grade you can overturn: if the other reading is right for your system, say so, and the next run inherits your answer instead of guessing again.

Excluded apps/v4/registry/_legacy-base-colors.ts (1,113 decls), apps/v4/registry/_legacy-colors.ts (1,200 decls), apps/v4/registry/themes.ts (840 decls) and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css (439 decls) from the declared token system.
run.token_count from a raw discovery figure of 1,185 concepts down to 40 canonical tokens; single-source, coverage and orphans all graded against the smaller, real system instead of being swamped by catalog data.
single-source · coverage · orphans
All four files are reachable from owned production entry points and declaration-shaped, so a stricter reading of 'discover every candidate, prove it ships' would inventory them as canonical sources the same as globals.css.
Reported a deduplicated, collapsed canonical token count (40) as run.token_count, not the raw discover_tokens.py concept count for globals.css (93) or the theoretical alias_of-is-null count (35).
The headline count away from double-counting Tailwind v4's own '@theme inline' pattern: 53 of the 93 raw concepts are same-file CSS-custom-property aliases (e.g. concept 'primary' and concept 'color-primary', the latter's sole value being 'var(--primary)') that discover_tokens.py's projection-collapse rule does not yet fold into their canonical concept — that rule currently covers only SCSS-to-CSS-custom-property compilation. This run applied that collapse by hand for tokens.filtered.json, merging each alias's site onto its canonical concept as a 'projected_from' entry. chart-1..5 (family 'color') were kept as their own canonical concepts rather than collapsed, because their alias target (--color-blue-300..800) is Tailwind's own default palette, not a name declared in this file — references/vitals.md's framework-default rule counts a project's own reference to a framework default as the project's token. font-sans/font-heading/font-mono were excluded rather than counted, because their @theme-inline declaration is self-referential (alias_of == its own id) — a passthrough for a next/font runtime-injected value, not a static definition.
report
A stricter, literal reading of the tool's own concept list would report 93 (no collapsing) or 35 (collapsing only alias_of-is-null concepts, which would incorrectly also drop chart-1..5).
Excluded 20 'canonical' concepts discover_tokens.py found outside globals.css (apps/v4/lib/font-definitions.ts, hooks/use-meta-color.ts, app/layout.tsx, app/(view)/preview/typeset/layout.tsx, and several font-loader helper files) from the token count.
token_count away from counting non-token JS object properties as design tokens, and stack.token_sources down to the one file the project actually declares its design tokens in.
report
Inspecting each: 'opengraph.width'/'opengraph.height' are literal OpenGraph image pixel dimensions (app/layout.tsx:45-46), 'icons.icon' is a favicon file path (app/layout.tsx:59), 'meta-theme-colors.dark'/'meta-theme-colors.light' are PWA theme-color meta values (hooks/use-meta-color.ts:5-6), and the rest (label/name/title/variable/registryvariable/previewvariable/value) are internal property names inside a custom font-loader's metadata records (lib/font-definitions.ts) — none is a name a component author would type in place of a value. The conservative-js-theme-object extractor currently has no shape heuristic to tell a real token map from an arbitrary data object; this is a tool limitation worth fixing, not a project finding.
Graded leakage 'pass' rather than 'attention', though a real uncovered finding exists (#000000 x 24 in packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css) and a large pool of literals (214 bracket-arbitrary px/rem values, near-miss overall) is unreviewed.
The mechanical grade follows references/vitals.md's stated rule exactly: leakage's pass/attention/fail line reads only the redundant tier, and audit_literal_colors.py found zero redundant and zero exact-value-candidate findings across the 13 consumer stylesheets it scanned.
leakage
A reader could reasonably want 'attention' here so the grade itself flags that something is unresolved, rather than relying on this note and the uncovered-tier listing to carry that signal — near-miss stayed unmeasured for color, and Tailwind bracket-arbitrary literals in .tsx (where the shimmer-color-[#378ADD] finding and the 214 unreviewed dimension literals both live) are outside what audit_literal_colors.py scans at all.
Graded mode-completeness from an agent reading apps/v4/app/globals.css's :root (line 99) and .dark (line 143) blocks directly, side by side, rather than from a tool-verified compiled or runtime artifact.
mode-completeness to 'pass' with real file:line evidence, instead of 'blocked' — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured (the generic engine has no CSS-source-pairing check, only a build/runtime-artifact one), so a strict reading of the vitals.md instruction ('graded only where compiled or resolved output exists') would leave this blocked.
mode-completeness
references/vitals.md's mode-completeness signal is stated as 'the set difference across mode blocks' without requiring compiled output specifically (unlike coverage's framework-default rule, which is explicit about needing a checked version) — reading source blocks directly is a legitimate way to compute that set difference, and the original run against this same repository did the same thing.
The eight vitals

Eight checks on your token system

Each check is graded on its own, against evidence pulled from your repository. There is no single overall score, because averaging these would hide the one thing you need to see. If your system has no dark mode, that check is marked not applicable rather than counted against you. And if a check could not run at all, it says blocked instead of quietly passing.

not-visible

tier integrity

This repository has no distinct primitive layer to skip: `--primary` is a role name holding a concrete value (globals.css:107 light, :150 dark), so discovery classifies it `primitive` on its value shape. 59 of 101 component token references reach a concept tiered `primitive`, but that number measures the absence of a primitive layer rather than components bypassing a semantic one. Grading it would report a finding the evidence does not support. apps/v4/app/globals.css:107

not-visible

leakage

0 exact-value candidate groups and 1 uncovered candidate groups were measured across 13 owned reachable consumer styles, but semantic equivalence and near misses remain unmeasured.

watch

coverage

9 of 11 categories present, verified against tailwindcss@4.3.0 as pinned in pnpm-lock.yaml. color, typography, space, size, radius, border, elevation, motion and breakpoint all resolve to a real token — a project token in globals.css, or a Tailwind v4 default-theme token the project imports and never overrides. z-index and opacity do not: Tailwind v4 ships no theme namespace for either, and the project declares neither. apps/v4/app/globals.css:99

not-visible

mode completeness

Two modes are declared and both have a mechanism — `@custom-variant dark` at globals.css:41 and a `.dark` block at :143. No resolved output was inspected for either, so this run cannot say whether every token that resolves in light also resolves in dark. An audit gap, not a finding about the codebase. apps/v4/app/globals.css:143

healthy

naming coherence

One grammar per syntax. 679 kebab-case and 500 single-word names across the CSS custom properties and JSON, and the 6 camelCase names are JS object keys, which cannot hold a hyphen. Counted across syntaxes this would read as two grammars and grade the language rather than the system. apps/v4/app/globals.css:99

not-visible

single source

102 concepts carry more than one value, and this run cannot tell a variant from a duplicate. 32 are one `:root` value and one `.dark` value in globals.css — a mode pair, not a duplication. 44 more are in registry/themes.ts, which declares roughly ten selectable themes, and 6 in the legacy base-colour registries do the same. Grading duplication here would report a design intent as a defect. apps/v4/app/globals.css:107

healthy

orphans

1 of 69 stylesheets (1.45%) holds token declarations no owned production entry reaches — `apps/v4/public/r/themes.css`, a generated registry artifact served rather than imported. Ten further orphans fall outside the owned scope and are kept visible rather than counted. apps/v4/public/r/themes.css:1

not-visible

enforcement

No rule reads the token layer. `pnpm lint` in code-check.yml runs ESLint, and the repository ships no stylelint config and no token-aware rule, so nothing stops a raw hex from being added to a component tomorrow. With nothing in place there is nothing to verify as protected, which is why this vital's worst outcome is `not-visible` rather than `needs-work`. .github/workflows/code-check.yml:1

Pass — checked, nothing to fix Attention — worth a look, not urgent Fail — real problems with a clear fix Blocked — could not check this one N/A — does not apply to your setup

Where each token comes from

A chain runs primitive definition to semantic alias to custom-property projection to the components that use it. The chain is what separates a deliberate alias from a duplicate definition: two names for one value with a link between them is the system working, and two names without one is drift. A dashed step is a link this run could not trace.

Mode completeness

Which tokens are missing a value in each mode

When a token has a value in one mode but not another, nothing breaks at build time. It quietly falls back, renders wrong, and ships. These gaps do not show up anywhere else in the report.

Mode coverage is source-limited. 20 bundle × mode × family cells are recorded: 4 blocked · 5 measured · 9 not_applicable · 2 unmeasured. No source-only declaration is promoted to compiled runtime proof.
No mode gaps are claimed. Provide compiled output for every registered bundle and scheme before individual missing values are graded.
Orphans & enforcement

Tokens nothing uses, and what stops this coming back

Orphaned tokens make your system look bigger and more capable than it really is. They stick around because nothing breaks when they go, so nobody ever gets a reason to remove them.

Orphan measurement

healthy

1 of 69 stylesheets (1.45%) holds token declarations no owned production entry reaches — `apps/v4/public/r/themes.css`, a generated registry artifact served rather than imported. Ten further orphans fall outside the owned scope and are kept visible rather than counted.

What protects this today

not-visible

No rule reads the token layer. `pnpm lint` in code-check.yml runs ESLint, and the repository ships no stylelint config and no token-aware rule, so nothing stops a raw hex from being added to a component tomorrow. With nothing in place there is nothing to verify as protected, which is why this vital's worst outcome is `not-visible` rather than `needs-work`.

Measurement

How this was measured

Two runs against the same repository should be able to agree, or at least explain why they don't. This is what makes that possible: the exact sources this run counted as tokens, the scope and file count it searched for leaks, the adapters it detected and how sure it was, and any framework version it had to check before grading coverage. Recorded here, a difference between two runs points at a fact instead of an argument.

Measured scope

2 profiles proved 31 product roots: 31 owned and 0 unresolved in ownership. The full graph reaches 3314 files; the owned graph reaches 3314. 1 actionable imports remain unresolved. All 5837 classified import misses remain visible by reason: 1 dynamic runtime import; 5836 external package. 1185 canonical concepts came from 18 confirmed definition sources, and 9 candidate or override sources were held out.

Unification strategy

How to turn this audit into a durable system

The recommendation below separates the system of design decisions from the system of component implementation. It uses this repository's framework boundaries, delivery mechanisms, token inventory, modes, and component adoption to choose a model, then defines the architecture, rollout gates, standards, and measures that fit the evidence.

token-led-hybrid — Unify decisions everywhere; unify components where ownership is proven.

This run found 1185 canonical concepts across 18 confirmed token-definition sources, 5 components with confirmed token usage, 2 active framework profiles, and 2 styling or framework adapters. A repository-wide component replacement would cross framework behavior and upgrade boundaries that this token audit does not measure. Use one semantic token contract across them, preserve framework-specific delivery adapters, and reserve shared component implementation for owned surfaces.

Guardrails

  • Keep one hand-authored source of truth; generate every projection.
  • Consume semantic tokens by default and document every primitive exception.
  • Treat framework adapters as translation boundaries, not parallel design systems.
  • Prove every declared mode in compiled or runtime output before claiming coverage.
  • Never infer that token consistency proves component behavior or accessibility.
  • Version public contracts and deprecate before removing or renaming them.
Component boundary: This audit does not measure behavior, public APIs, localization, state, analytics, authorization, or interaction accessibility. Complete a separate component-contract assessment before proposing repository-wide replacement.

Why component-first unification is risky

Framework and ownership boundaries

Evidence now: 2 active framework profiles; 31 of 31 production roots are proven owned.

Implication: A global component replacement can turn upstream upgrades into long-lived fork maintenance. Preserve framework-owned behavior and markup until a component-contract assessment proves a safe boundary.

Multiple delivery mechanisms

Evidence now: 18 confirmed token-definition sources feed 2 styling or framework adapters.

Implication: Unify the decisions in one typed graph, then generate compatible projections. Requiring every framework to share one runtime format would couple design governance to implementation history.

Behavioral contracts exceed styling

Evidence now: 5 components with confirmed token usage; behavior, public APIs, localization, state, analytics, authorization, and interaction accessibility remain outside this audit.

Implication: Token adoption can align visual decisions without proving that shared component code is interchangeable. Assess those contracts separately before consolidation.

Runtime modes need compiled proof

Evidence now: 2 modes are declared and 0 bundle-by-mode pairs are resolved.

Implication: Source declarations prove intent, while compiled or runtime values prove delivery. Keep mode claims blocked until every production pair has evidence.

Migration requires governance

Evidence now: Enforcement is graded not-visible and 4 capabilities remain blocked or unmeasured.

Implication: A token package alone will not stop new drift. Pair migration with ownership, versioning, deprecation, CI gates, and measurable exit criteria.

Target architecture

1. One canonical contract

Author one typed token graph for 1185 concepts; generate every other representation instead of maintaining parallel sources.

2. Semantic decisions

Map primitives to product intent such as text, surface, action, focus, and status. Require components to consume semantics by default.

3. Generated delivery adapters

Project the contract through tailwind, css-vars. Keep framework translation separate from the design decisions it carries.

4. Shared components for owned surfaces

Build versioned components for new and product-owned surfaces; let existing framework components adopt the same semantic contract without requiring shared markup.

5. Governance and proof

Version public contracts, deprecate before removal, validate every declared mode and production bundle, and reject regressions in CI.

Rollout plan

Phase 0 · Prove the boundary

Resolve production reachability, ownership, and the evidence gaps that would make later adoption claims unreliable.

Evidence now: 1 unresolved import; 4 capabilities still blocked or unmeasured.

Exit when: Every actionable import is resolved or explicitly exempted, production roots are proven, and remaining unknowns are named as unmeasured.

Phase 1 · Freeze identity and semantics

Confirm brand identity, then define primitive, semantic, and optional component tiers with ownership and mode policies.

Evidence now: Typography identity is not-visible; brand color identity is not-visible.

Exit when: Every governed token has a type, description, owner, semantic role, and declared mode behavior.

Phase 2 · Choose one source and generate adapters

Make one token graph authoritative and generate runtime, legacy, and framework-specific projections.

Evidence now: 1185 concepts currently span 18 token-bearing sources and 2 adapters.

Exit when: No projection is independently authored, aliases resolve without cycles, and primitive-to-consumer lineage is traceable.

Phase 3 · Prove modes and bundles

Compile or resolve every declared mode across each production bundle and verify the resulting values, not only their source declarations.

Evidence now: 2 declared modes; 0 resolved bundle-by-mode pairs. No declared mode mechanism or resolved output was inspected.

Exit when: The coverage matrix contains no unexplained blocked cell and every declared mode has compiled or runtime evidence.

Phase 4 · Migrate by impact

Pilot the semantic contract on the highest-usage owned component or production surface; replace only decisions whose semantic role is proven.

Evidence now: 5 components using tokens was measured; start with v4 / chart-area-interactive.

Exit when: The pilot passes visual, accessibility, mode, and regression checks without changing component behavior or public APIs.

Phase 5 · Enforce and expand

Prevent new drift, publish deprecation rules, and expand shared components only where ownership and component contracts are proven.

Evidence now: Enforcement is graded not-visible; leakage baseline: redundant not-visible, exact-value candidate 0, near-miss not-visible, uncovered not-visible, uncovered candidate 1.

Exit when: CI rejects invalid aliases, missing modes, inaccessible resolved pairs, unapproved literals, and public removals without deprecation.
